Jeez Show less Read more Like 6 Dislike Reply @m1LckyW4Y 3 months ago Hollywood isn’t “moving to YouTube”, it’s crawling there after years of setting fire to its own audience with preachy scripts, moral lectures from people who fly private, and an endless parade of scandals exposing Tinseltown as a glitter-covered HR nightmare. The loyal movie fans didn’t mysteriously vanish, they were actively chased off by films that hate them, lectures disguised as entertainment, and an industry more interested in ticking ideological boxes than telling a half-decent story. Add to that the recurring revelations about who’s been doing what to whom behind closed doors, and suddenly the red carpet looks less glamorous and more like a police cordon. So yes, stream the Oscars on YouTube, right between influencer drama and apology videos, because that’s exactly where an industry goes when the magic is gone, the trust is shattered, and the audience would rather rewatch a 90s blockbuster than be scolded by a millionaire in a tuxedo. Show less Read more Like 4 Dislike Reply @TheSpaLife69 3 months ago Hardly anything is even broadcast in a studio these days either. The way Will Smith was able to enjoy the rest of the show after THE SLAP said a lot about Hollywood. Who wants to watch a bunch of rich people award themselves when regular hard working people can't afford to pay their electricity bill.
